quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Does making eye contact with other drivers mean they see you?

options.text: Yes, it means they see you.
Yes, and they will yield to you.
No, it does not mean they see you.
No, and it is not worth trying.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact. A driver may look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or put them in saddlebags. High loads raise the center of gravity and make the motorcycle unbalanced. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from wind while riding?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Which lane position should you use when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Always stay away from the left portion.
Always stay away from the right portion.
Always stay away from the center portion.

questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases you?

options.text: Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Slow down, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. Downshift and approach slowly. Then accelerate and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight away from other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Use vehicles ahead of you for clues about the road. Their lights help you see ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle passes you from behind?

options.text: Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is safest when being passed. Staying close to the passing vehicle risks a crash. Staying far from it may make the driver cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers, applying firm and smooth pressure gradually.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars tightly and close the throttle slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars tightly and close the throttle slowly.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, lean forward, and pull off the road. Avoid using the brakes, as they can make wobbling worse.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time. The safest lane position changes too. Pick the position that gives you the most space around you and helps other drivers see you clearly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or tough material. You should also wear footwear that covers and supports your ankles and hearing protection, even if you wear a helmet.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: Motorcyclists may use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes:

options.text: Only if they are carrying a passenger.

questions.explanation: In Utah, motorcyclists can use designated HOV lanes at any time. The number of riders on the motorcycle does not matter.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets the rider touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Has a seat level with the rider's waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the rider touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets your feet reach the ground while you sit on it. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass you. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should only be used when the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of total braking power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: Passengers should always lean with the rider when turning. Avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle. In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit the view of the motorcycle operator.
Allow the operator to see far to the sides as needed.
Do not need to be worn if the operator thinks their view would be limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the operator to see far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit their side vision, but this is not true. Any approved helmet lets the operator see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the strongest stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to doing so in a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Passing techniques are the same for motorcycles and cars. But motorcycles are harder to see. Your motorcycle can easily hide in another vehicle's blind spot. Other drivers may not notice you even when looking.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following, except:

options.text: The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread, and the condition of your tire sidewalls and treads.

questions.question: For routine braking:

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.
